title: Counters (つ・人・本・枚・匹・冊・台・杯・回・階)
meaning: Numbers must be followed by a counter matching the type of object.
simpleExplanation: In Japanese you cannot just say "three"; you need a counter word that matches what you count. つ for general things (三つ), 人 for people (三人), 本 for long thin things (bottles, pens), 枚 for flat things (paper, tickets), 匹 for small animals, 冊 for books, 台 for machines, 杯 for cups, 回 for times, 階 for floors. The number + counter usually sits right before the verb: りんごを三つください.
whenUsed: Shopping, ordering, describing your family, counting anything. Some readings change: 一人 ひとり, 二人 ふたり, 一本 いっぽん, 三本 さんぼん, 一匹 いっぴき, 一杯 いっぱい, 一冊 いっさつ.
formation: Noun + を／が + Number + counter + verb　(the counter phrase usually sits right before the verb)

similarGrammar.difference: Number + counter goes before あります／います: 学生が三人います.

commonMistakes.why: People take 人, not つ.

commonMistakes.wrong: ビールを二つ (in a bar, for bottles)
commonMistakes.why: Bottles are 本, glasses are 杯. (二つ is understood but not the tested form.)

commonMistakes.wrong: 四人 read as しにん
commonMistakes.why: 四人 is always よにん.

usageNotes: Key irregulars: 一人（ひとり）, 二人（ふたり）, 四人（よにん）; 一本（いっぽん）, 三本（さんぼん）, 六本（ろっぽん）; 一枚（いちまい）; 一匹（いっぴき）, 三匹（さんびき）; 一冊（いっさつ）; 一台（いちだい）; 一杯（いっぱい）, 三杯（さんばい）; 一階（いっかい）, 三階（さんがい）. Native numbers ひとつ〜とお (十) for general objects; ask "how many" with いくつ／何人／何本 etc.
jlptTips: Match the counter to the object: paper/tickets → 枚, pens/bottles → 本, books → 冊, animals → 匹, people → 人, cars/machines → 台.
Reading questions test ひとり, ふたり, よにん, いっぽん, さんぼん, いっぴき, いっぱい.
